items.title: Morning Briefing: Oct. 31, 2026
items.excerpt: Here's a rundown of all the news you need to start Saturday, including Polish President Karol Nawrocki aborting an Africa trip and returning to Warsaw as a power struggle erupts over control of the Constitutional Tribunal; Türkiye formally nominating OSCE Secretary-General Feridun Sinirlioglu as a candidate for UN secretary-general; and the US State Department approving a possible $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 MSE missiles to Ukraine. Polish President Karol Nawrocki aborted a flight to Senegal and returned to Warsaw as rival groups of judges disputed control of the Constitutional Tribunal, after orders appeared on its website to temporarily remove its president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, and vice president Bartlomiej Sochanski, in a move the tribunal rejected as illegal and a "coup." Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska said she ordered the two to stop their duties, while police said they were deployed for possible threats to judges and had not entered the building. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said "restoring the rule of law is our duty," while opposition Law and Justice leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski called the events a "coup against the Constitutional Tribunal." Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski defended the police action as aimed at letting duly elected judges resume the court’s work, while US Ambassador Tom Rose urged restraint, calling the situation "very serious." ## Türkiye nominates OSCE chief Sinirlioglu as candidate for next UN secretary-general Türkiye formally nominated Feridun Sinirlioglu, secretary-general of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, as a candidate for UN secretary-general, after the latest Security Council straw poll ended inconclusively, according to Turkish Foreign Ministry sources. ... ## US approves $2.1B Patriot missile sale to Ukraine The US State Department approved a possible sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement missiles and related equipment to Ukraine at an estimated cost of $2.1 billion, saying the cost is "funded entirely by partners and allies" and that "no US funds are involved in this sale." Ukraine will pay with donations from Canada, Germany and Norway via the JUMPSTART program and national funds financed by the EU’s Ukraine Support Loan, according to the agency, with Lockheed Martin as principal contractor. The approval comes days after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine has received an average of 12 Patriot interceptors per month from the US this year, while needing to intercept around 150 Russian ballistic missiles per month.

items.title: While You Were Sleeping: 5 stories you might have missed, Oct 31, 2026 | The Straits Times
items.excerpt: ## ‘Anchor the ground’: Canada, EU launch new alliance The EU and Canada announced an alliance on Oct 30 aimed at cementing their own relations in the face of President Donald Trump’s moves to tear up US ties with its old partners. Canada agreed to contribute to a €90 billion (S$128 billion) support loan for Ukraine and work closer with Brussels on anything from critical minerals to artificial intelligence, after a two-day summit in Montreal. “The world’s becoming more dangerous and divided. Our societies are being shaken by new storms,” Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told a press conference, mentioning eroding democratic norms and “the weaponisation of trade.” “Together, Canada and the European Union are anchoring the ground. Anchoring our ground to uphold our values while forming a protective canopy under which our citizens can all thrive,” he said, after talks with EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa. ## Nations agree push to get nature goals on track ... Nearly 200 nations on Oct 30 adopted hard-fought agreements at a UN biodiversity summit aimed at putting the world back on track in efforts to halt nature’s destruction by 2030. Delegates cheered as the crucial texts were approved in overtime following two weeks of tense negotiations at the COP17 conference in Armenia’s capital Yerevan. “And that’s it. Perfect,” said COP17 president Hambardzum Matevosyan to applause, as he brought down the gavel on the documents, the final versions of which were not immediately available. ## US midterm early voting hits record 48 million PHOTO: EPA A record 47.9 million Americans have already voted in next week’s US midterm elections, with participation surging in key battleground states and registered Democrats outpacing Republicans, figures showed Oct 30. The University of Florida’s Election Lab had recorded 47,922,669 early votes nationwide by midday, surpassing the previous midterm record of 45.9 million cast ahead of Election Day in 2022. The surge is especially pronounced in states with fiercely contested Senate races that could determine control of the chamber during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s presidency.

items.title: PCE inflation report September 2026:
items.excerpt: Published Thu, Oct 29 2026 8:32 AM EDT Updated Thu, Oct 29 2026 2:06 PM EDT ... Key Points - The U.S. economy grew at a 3.4% pace in the third quarter, faster than expected. - Inflation continued to run above the Fed's 2% target in September, with a headline rate of 3.6% and core at 3.1%, according to the central bank's preferred gauge. - Consumer ... Personal income increased just 0.2%. ... The pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department reports Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.5% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.6%. The monthly increase was the largest since March but in line with the Dow Jones consensus, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below. Excluding food and energy, the core PCE posted respective readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, in line with the consensus. While the Fed follows both measures closely, officials generally see the core reading as more indicative of longer-term inflation trends. While inflation continued to run ahead of the Fed's 2% target, the Commerce Department also reported that gross domestic product was strong in the third quarter. GDP increased at a seasonally adjusted annualized pace of 3.4%, better than the 3.1% estimate and well ahead of the 2.2% in the second quarter. Also, in September consumer spending proved resilient, climbing 0.5%, a bit below the forecast for a 0.6% gain, while personal income rose 0.2%, compared with the estimate for 0.3%. The reports come the day after the Fed voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75%-4%. Despite elevated inflation readings, central bank officials insist they can afford to evaluate incoming data before deciding on their next move. "The period right in front of us is information rich. There is a lot that's happening in the world. My colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said Wednesday. However, the data deluge from Thursday shows the Fed could have more work to do. ... Consumer spending rose 3.8% in the third quarter, the same pace as the prior period. Gross private domestic investment soared 19.4%, driven by a 20.9% surge in equipment spending and an 8.4% jump on intellectual property products. Real sales to private domestic purchasers, a proxy that Fed officials use for underlying demand, rose 4.9%, compared with a 4.6% increase in the second quarter. There was some good inflation news for the period: On a quarterly basis, PCE prices rose 2.1% on the headline number and 2.5% for core, down respectively from 5% and 3.3% in the second quarter. September's price increases were driven largely by a surge in energy costs that economists fear could be spreading to other parts of the economy. Gasoline and other energy goods saw a 9.2% rise for the month while energy goods and services broadly jumped 5.4%. At the same time, services prices excluding energy and housing rose 0.4%, and housing costs increased 0.3%.

items.title: Inflation heats up again, days before midterm elections | PBS News
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON (AP) — An inflation gauge closely monitored by the Federal Reserve accelerated last month, showing that prices remain elevated less than a week before midterm elections in which the uncomfortably high cost of living for millions of Americans has become a central issue. Consumer prices rose 3.6% in September from a year earlier, the Commerce Department said Thursday, up from 3.4% in August. On a monthly basis, prices climbed 0.5%, up from 0.3% in August and the highest figure since May. Rising gas prices drove much of the inflation increase as renewed violence in the Middle East has kept oil prices above $100 a barrel, up from below $70 before the Iran war. But prices also rose outside of fuel costs. The cost of services such as shipping, hotel rooms, and utilities increased rapidly from August to September, a sign that inflation is spreading and growing more entrenched.

items.title: 2026 elections live updates as Trump rallies Florida voters, El-Sayed clashes with Stevens
items.excerpt: ## What to know as Election Day approaches for the 2026 midterms: - With just three days to go until Election Day, Tuesday, Nov. 3, candidates in key Senate and House elections are making their closing arguments to midterm voters. - President Trump held a rally in Florida, continuing a weekslong blitz. He reversed course and said he will hold rallies in Kansas and Ohio this weekend. - The DOJ pushed to segregate some Alaska Senate ballots, pending a probe into how a man with nearly the same name as GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan ended up on the ballot. Democrat Mary Peltola denied involvement. - A California judge late Friday issued a temporary restraining order directing the federal government to stop demanding that California state and local election officials separate out ballots or not count certain votes from alleged noncitizens. The judge also ordered the DOJ to stop threatening officials with criminal prosecution if they do not comply. - Democratic Michigan Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed clashed with former primary rival Haley Stevens. - The latest CBS News polling shows Democrats with an edge in the House — but the Senate could hinge on toss-up elections in Maine, Ohio, Texas and more. CBS News now rates South Carolina as a GOP-leaning battleground. ... ## In intra-party feud, El-Sayed says Stevens "seems intent on relitigating a primary that ended three months ago" Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate candidate, hit back at Rep. Haley Stevens, whom he defeated in the primary, after she demanded an apology for comments he made about Israel. The dispute between the former Democratic rivals comes two days before they are expected to appear at an event in Detroit with Rep. James Clyburn of South Carolina — marking one of their only joint appearances since the contentious primary. In a statement Friday night, El-Sayed says his former rival "seems intent on relitigating a primary that ended three months ago" instead of focusing on beating the Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers and addressing Michiganders' cost of living concerns. Stevens said in an earlier statement Friday she planned to appear with El-Sayed on the campaign trail, but she expected him to apologize for comments about Israel and condemn an ad from an outside PAC that she said was antisemitic. She also wanted El-Sayed to take down his own ad featuring Tucker Carlson. "Abdul promises to get money out of politics," she said. "He can begin by getting Israel out of his explanation for everything Michigan cannot afford."

items.title: US midterms: 3 days to go – What latest polls say as early voting surges | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
items.excerpt: With three days to go before the US midterm elections, Democrats are leading national polls as millions of Americans cast their ballots early. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump has announced he will carry on with his campaigns in Kansas and Iowa as both parties make their final push ahead of Election Day on Tuesday. ... ## What do the US midterm polls say? According to RealClearPolling’s latest national congressional ballot average, Democrats still lead Republicans by 8.2 percentage points. Democrats lead by 51.4 percent to 43.2 percent. A separate Economist/YouGov survey released on Thursday found that 44 percent of registered voters expect Democrats to control the House of Representatives after the election, compared with 31 percent who expect Republicans to retain control. Expectations were much closer for the Senate, with 39 percent expecting a Democratic majority and 36 percent a Republican one. Kyle Kondik, managing editor of Sabato’s Crystal Ball at the University of Virginia Center for Politics, told Al Jazeera that the Democratic lead in national polling suggests a different picture for the two chambers. “A big Democratic lead in House generic ballot polling suggests that the House is almost certain to flip to Democrats,” Kondik said. “However, that does not mean the Senate is going to flip – it certainly could, but it is much more up in the air.” ## How many Americans have already voted? According to an Associated Press analysis released on Friday, more than 43 million Americans had voted early in person or returned mail ballots five days before Election Day. That’s nearly 10 million more than at the same point before the 2022 midterms, with some of the biggest increases recorded in states having competitive Senate races. In Texas, more than 6.3 million people had voted early as of Wednesday, compared with 4.2 million at the same point in 2022, an increase of 50 percent. ... However, early turnout figures don’t show which candidates voters have chosen or what the final results will be.

items.excerpt: - AP - Oct 31, 2026 - 4 hrs ago ... Houdini’s centennial spotlight: A newly published essay and a fresh fight over when and how he died NEW YORK (AP) — Harry Houdini, a century after his death, continues to captivate. A rare essay by the escape artist has been published, shedding light on his early influences. A recent book revisits questions about the cause and date of his death. Houdini, born Erik Weisz, became an international celebrity known for his escape acts. His mysterious death on Halloween 1926 remains debated, with new theories challenging the official cause. Centennial events this weekend include a "Grand Houdini Centenarium" in Budapest, an auction in Hollywood, and seances in Chicago and Maryland. Despite the intrigue, experts say his legacy endures through his remarkable life. LOS ANGELES (AP) — Scott Clifton of “The Bold and the Beautiful” and Tamara Tunie of “Beyond the Gates” have won lead acting honors at the Daytime Emmy Awards. It's Clifton's second career trophy in the lead category. Tunie made her return to the soap opera genre after 17 years away. “General Hospital” won its record 19th trophy overall as outstanding drama and sixth in a row. Roger Howarth and Beth Maitland of “The Young and the Restless” swept the supporting acting categories. Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, lost in the lifestyle program category for her former Netflix show “With Love, Meghan.” NEW YORK (AP) — Actor Margaret Qualley and Grammy winner Jack Antonoff have filed for divorce after three years of marriage. Court records show the case was filed Friday in Kings County Supreme Court in New York as an uncontested matrimonial action. Qualley is listed as the plaintiff, and Antonoff as the defendant. The couple separated in July. Qualley, 32, is known for films like “The Substance” and “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.” Antonoff, 42, is a 14-time Grammy-winning songwriter and producer. The couple began dating in 2021 and married in August 2023. NEW YORK (AP) — Kirk Franklin is back with his new album, "I Am What I Am," out Friday. His 14th studio project and first double album, 14 tracks are divided between contemporary music and traditional, live-recorded gospel songs. Features include gospel royalty Karen Clark Sheard and star mainstream artists like Jelly Roll, Davido and GloRilla. “This Time," featuring GloRilla, hit No. 1 on Billboard’s hot gospel songs, extending Franklin's record to ten No. 1s on the chart. Known for his crossover hits, the 20-time Grammy winner has frequently faced criticism for working with secular artists, but remains unapologetic in the name of spreading his Christian faith. WASHINGTON (AP) — First Walter Koenig, who played Ensign Pavel Chekov in the original series during the 1960s, died at age 90. Then, three days later, the cosmos lost Patrick Stewart. The Shakespearean actor in 1987 became Capt. Jean-Luc Picard, the unlikely and poetic face of that show’s sequel, “Star Trek: The Next Generation.” For a fan base that has long signed on as acolytes of a brighter, more equitable future, recent days have made the present sting. William Shatner played Capt. James T. Kirk in the original series in the 1960s. He called it a “heartbreaking week.” ... MIAMI BEACH, Fla. (AP) — Prosecutors have dropped a felony charge against rapper Rick Ross a month after he was arrested in Miami Beach when a woman he was living with told police he hit her. The Miami-Dade State Attorney’s Office filed paperwork Thursday to drop a felony charge of battery by strangulation because of “insufficient evidence.” Ross, whose legal name is William Roberts II, still faces a misdemeanor charge of battery domestic violence. Ross has pleaded not guilty to all charges.
